title: Tiered input/output token rates + streaming & minimums experiment
creator: Ana Morales
description: Run an experiment to evaluate tiered input vs output token pricing, streaming surcharge, and minimums for the Hosted API. The goal is to find pricing rules that (a) better reflect compute cost asymmetry between input and output tokens for large models and streaming, (b) reduce noise from low-usage accounts via sensible minimums, and (c) surface enterprise-friendly contract options that map to the security questionnaire (SLA, audit logs, data residency). This ticket captures the experiment matrix, measurement plan, stakeholder alignment, and follow-up rollout requirements.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Experiment matrix deployed to billing sandbox and sampling fleet; 2) Clear measurement dashboard capturing ARPU, churn delta for cohorts, average request latency, and per-token margin; 3) Legal and Sales signoff on negotiable minimum tiers for enterprise contracts; 4) Security questionnaire implications documented and flagged for Private/Dedicated customers; 5) Recommendation memo and rollout plan (canary + rollback) delivered to leadership.
comments: 2025-02-18 — Ana Morales: Created ticket. Initial problem statement and goals laid out. Suggested split-tests: (A) symmetric pricing baseline, (B) input-weighted pricing, (C) output-weighted pricing with streaming surcharge, (D) monthly minimum tiers. Asked Eng for cost model inputs and Design for communication mockups.

2025-02-21 — Ravi Patel: Aligned on metrics. Primary metrics: ARPU (30d), conversion to paid, churn 90d, margin per 1M tokens. Secondary: request latency impact, customer support volume. Tagged ENG and Legal for dependencies.

2025-02-25 — Mateo Chen (Eng): ENG-3345 tracking cost-per-token telemetry. Estimated 3 sprints to instrument sampling fleet. Noted: streaming increases server-side concurrency; recommend separate surcharge rather than per-token multiplier. Added as dependency.

2025-02-28 — Priya Singh (Legal): Reviewed high-level pricing matrix. Key ask: ensure contract minimum language is explicit about overage billing cadence and audit rights. Also flagged security questionnaire items: SOC2 evidence, KMS integration, and data retention policy must be present for enterprise tiers.

2025-03-03 — Design review (DES-204): Mockups for billing page and pricing modal reviewed. Highlight: clearly show input vs output token split on invoices and provide example usage scenarios for streaming. Designer requested sample invoice data from Finance.

2025-03-05 — Ravi Patel: Updated experiment timeline and opened PR for measurement dashboard. Next steps: finalize experiment price points, create billing sandbox promo codes, and schedule sales enablement session to surface changes to enterprise AE motion.
experiment_matrix: Variant A: baseline symmetric (0.0006 per input, 0.0006 per output); Variant B: input-discount (0.0004 input / 0.0007 output); Variant C: output-premium + streaming surcharge (0.0005 input / 0.0009 output + $0.0002/sec-streaming); Variant D: symmetric with monthly minimums [$50, $500, $5k] mapped to usage tiers. Run for 30 days per cohort. Randomize new signups and existing customers into cohorts where contract allows.
measurement_plan: Instrument per-request input_token_count, output_token_count, streaming_seconds, model_type, customer_tier. Track: revenue per customer, tokens per session, sessions per month, latency P95, error rate, churn at 30/90 days, sales objections logged. Use sandbox billing sandbox IDs and a 5% traffic sample on production for live validation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers perceive change as price increase -> Mitigate by grandfathering active subscriptions for 90 days and offering credits; messaging emphasises alignment of price to compute cost. Risk: streaming surcharge increases latency due to concurrency -> Mitigate with autoscaling policy and early signal to engineering. Risk: enterprise contracts require custom minimums -> Mitigate by templated addenda for negotiated minimums and explicit audit language.
sales_and_legal_notes: Sales: prefer simple tiers for AE conversations; minimums should be negotiable but surfaced clearly in proposal templates. Legal: minimums must include clear billing cadence, termination, and audit rights. For security questionnaire, ensure we can provide SOC2 + KMS integration docs; surface any enterprise asks to Security team via SR ticket.
next_steps: 1) Engineering: finalize telemetry and billing sandbox (ENG-3345) by 2025-03-15; 2) Finance: seed sandbox with credit buckets and invoice examples; 3) Design: finalize pricing modal and invoice examples by 2025-03-10; 4) Legal & Sales: draft contract language and AE playbook by 2025-03-20; 5) Run 30-day experiment in staged cohorts starting 2025-03-25.
notes_for_engineering: Provide an API flag for billing variant (billing_variant) and emit telemetry tags (billing_variant, cohort_id). Ensure streaming_seconds is captured for partial responses. Billing pipeline must be able to apply per-variant multipliers and minimums. Coordinate with infra for concurrency and memory impact of streaming workloads.
implementation_constraints: Billing pipeline currently supports symmetric per-token buckets; we will need two new dimensions (input_token vs output_token) and a streaming_seconds meter. Changes must be backwards compatible for existing invoices. Estimate: 3 weeks of backend work + 1 week for QA and migrations.
post_experiment_decision_criteria: Recommend moving forward if: incremental margin on sampled traffic increases >=10% without >2% uplift in 30d churn; enterprise AE feedback rate neutral or positive; no significant latency regressions. Otherwise revert and iterate with adjusted price points.
customer_communications: Draft email for affected customers explaining rationale, example impact, and options (opt-out/grandfathering) plus FAQ. Require Design copy review and Legal signoff. AE playbook to include negotiation ammo and sample contract addenda.
audit_trail: Change log to be recorded in pricing repo and confluence. Billing experiments will create a temporary billing namespace (exp_pm_6210) and an audit log for every billed invoice showing variant applied. Security to review audit trail retention policy.
